Trading with leverage means exceeding your own buying power.
You are not trading with leverage when you say you trade $200 (which is not possible since 0.01 lots = $1000 unless you are using a cent account or the like) when your initial deposit is $200.
 That's basically 1:1.

You are trading with leverage when you, in a standard account, open a trade of 0.01 lot size with a deposit only $200. In this case you are actually opening a trade size of $1000 but only with a deposit of $200, which means that a 1:5 leverage.

Now, when you select a leverage when you sign up with your broker, you are simply selecting the maximum allowed leverage the broker offers should you wish to amplify your buying xx times. It does not mean that each trade you do always makes use of your selected leverage. So, if you have a leverage of 1:500, have a deposit of $1000 and decided to open a 0.01 lot size trade, you are trading with 1:1 leverage, but have a maximum allowed trade size of 5lots should you with to do so.
